Architecture: The college is recognized for its stunning, Gothic-inspired architecture.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My college has always stood out because of its strong infrastructure and well-planned campus environment. From spacious classrooms to well-equipped labs, everything is designed to make the learning experience smooth and productive. The campus atmosphere is clean, disciplined, and student-friendly. You genuinely feel like you're part of a professional and growing institution the moment you step inside.

Being from the Computer Science department, I had a very positive academic journey. The department is known for its dedicated faculty, supportive staff, and the practical exposure it provides to students. Teachers are approachable and always ready to help, whether it’s about assignments, projects, or career guidance. Other departments also maintain the same level of discipline and commitment, which reflects the overall quality of the college.

One thing I really appreciate about the college is the variety of events and activities it organizes throughout the year. Large festivals, technical events, cultural programs, and guest sessions with well-known personalities make the environment lively and inspiring. These events don’t just entertain students—they help us grow, network, and learn beyond the syllabus. The placement opportunities provided are also helpful for students who want to start their career right after graduation.

If there is one challenge, it is the college’s distance from the nearest station. Traveling daily can be tiring for many students because of the long commute. The canteen also has scope for improvement. But apart from these minor issues, the overall experience is truly valuable. The college has given me strong academic knowledge, great memories, and a sense of confidence for the future. I genuinely believe it’s a great place for students who want quality education and a supportive environment.

This college has a mixed reputation that prospective students should carefully evaluate before taking admission. Despite the hype surrounding its legacy name and CET cut-offs, the actual academic and campus experience often falls short.
Faculty quality is highly inconsistent. While a few professors are genuinely knowledgeable and supportive, many follow outdated teaching methods, are frequently absent, or lack understanding of current industry practices. There is significant academic misguidance, and in several cases, students are better off learning independently than being taught incorrect or irrelevant information.
Teacher politics is a serious issue. Internal favoritism, ego-driven behavior, and power dynamics often affect academic decisions, evaluations, and student growth. Instead of mentorship, some faculty members prioritize authority over learning, which creates an unhealthy academic environment.
Infrastructure and maintenance are poor for an institution of this stature. Washrooms frequently lack basic necessities such as functional door knobs, proper water systems, and cleanliness. Broken facilities and poor upkeep are common across the campus, reflecting a lack of accountability.
There is no formal or structured placement system. While the college does host events and benefits from being located in India’s commercial hub, any industry exposure or opportunities usually come from personal networking rather than institutional support.
On the positive side, students value the hands-on learning culture, exposure through events, peer-driven growth, and the advantage of studying in Mumbai, which offers access to studios, firms, and creative networks.
However, outdated teaching approaches, internal politics, poor infrastructure, and lack of clear guidance make this college a risky choice. If you can afford a well-run private college with updated curriculum, better facilities, and transparent academic systems, it may be a better investment.
Do not fall for the hype, rankings, or legacy reputation alone. Thorough research is essential before committing your crucial design education years here.

Suggestion- Before selecting this college, students do personally visit the campus, evaluate basic necessities like washrooms and infrastructure, assess the teaching staff’s mindset, and research carefully before committing.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Nayar
featured_reviews.review_text:
What should have been a review has become a eulogy, as I was just informed that Dr. Sampat is no more.

A great principal isn’t just a leader; they are a force. They shape minds, build character, and leave a mark so deep that even years later, their words echo in your heart.

Dr. Urmi Sampat was that kind of principal. She wasn’t just an educator,she was an institution.

I still remember my first day at H.J. College. She stood at the gate in a crisp cream saree, radiating authority yet warmth. “What’s your name?” she asked. “Namrata  , and I’m am going to be the topper this year,” I replied with pride. She just laughed and said, “Go and sit yourself inside.” That was Dr. Sampat, no fuss, no unnecessary praise, just straight to the point. But in that moment, she acknowledged me. And with her, an acknowledgment always meant something.

She had this aura about her,if she caught you in the corridor, you’d hold your breath. If you were exhaling, you wouldn’t dare inhale again until she passed. That was the kind of presence she had. But beneath that formidable exterior was someone who truly believed in her students.

I remember struggling in my psychology paper. She called me in and asked, “What the hell have you done?” I admitted, “I had a blackout.” She didn’t let me off easily. “I don’t believe in blackouts, but I believe in you,” she said. And that belief changed me. I promised her I wouldn’t let her down. And when I topped my methods, she awarded me the prestigious Miss H.J Title of the year. That moment shaped my future in ways I didn’t even realise at the time.

One of the greatest compliments I’ve ever received came from her:

Personally, I see a junior Dr. Urmi Sampat in Namrata.
That comparison still humbles me.

Everything she taught me stayed with me. From my first lesson at NPKT to my journey as a teacher at Arya Vidya Mandir Bandra, to moving to Dubai , her words have never left me. The discipline, the passion, the high standards,they are woven into the way I lead today.

I wish I had the chance to say goodbye. But in a way, someone like her never truly leaves. Somewhere, I know she’s making sure everyone arrives on time, does their job well, and carries themselves with the grace and dignity she expected of us all.

Dr. Sampat, you were the epitome of grace, excellence, and discipline. They don’t make them like you anymore. I treasured you, and I always will.
Yours truly,
Namrata Simon Nayar

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the legendary Sir J.J. School of Arts for a weekend sketch meet-up with Urban Sketchers Mumbai. The campus is dotted with sculptures and paintings created by students, quietly inhabiting every corner. Lush trees, the presence of many birds, and a heritage building—likely over a century old—give the place a timeless charm.
There is something about this institute that words struggle to capture. It seems to breathe artistic energy and passion. As I walked through the campus, I saw students deeply immersed in sculpting stone, shaping wood, and carving logs. Watching them so absorbed in their work felt like witnessing yogis in meditation—unaware of passersby, untouched by the world around them.
This heritage institute has nurtured some of the finest artists and architects in the country. Though I never had the fortune of studying here, I have learned immensely about art through colleagues and friends who are graduates of this institution.

From the very first day, the atmosphere of the department felt positive and inspiring. The campus environment encourages students to focus on learning while also exploring their own potential. The teachers use various teaching methods such as presentations, demonstrations, discussions, and problem-solving sessions. This helps students understand complex topics easily. As the saying goes, “Tell me and I forget, teach me and I remember, involve me and I learn.”
The laboratory sessions play a crucial role in pharmacy education, and the department excels in this area. The labs are well equipped with necessary instruments and materials. Practical sessions help students connect theory with practice. Performing experiments, preparing formulations, and learning laboratory techniques make students confident and competent. These experiences help us understand that “knowledge without practice is incomplete.”

One of the strongest pillars of the department is its faculty members. They are highly qualified, experienced, and approachable. Their dedication towards students is truly commendable. They not only teach from books but also share their personal experiences, which makes learning more meaningful. Teachers act not only as instructors but also as mentors and motivators. Whenever students face academic or personal challenges, the faculty provides guidance and emotional support. Truly, they believe that “a good teacher can change a life.”

“Every setback is a setup for a comeback” became my personal motto.

The friendships I made here, the guidance I received, and the experiences I gained will always remain close to my heart. The department became my second home, where I learned not only academic lessons but also life lessons. It taught me patience, perseverance, and professionalism.
Thank you SNDT

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Malvankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a student navigating the corridors of Mumbai University, I am compelled to share a deeply disappointing experience that reflects systemic neglect and administrative apathy.
Despite being one of the largest universities in India, the management here operates with alarming inefficiency. Students are routinely subjected to long queues, unresolved grievances, and a complete lack of accountability. The grievance redressal mechanism is virtually non-existent—when asked about it, staff either deny its existence or redirect students to the Board of Examinations, which itself remains inaccessible and unresponsive.
Staff members are frequently "on lunch break" or "in meetings," and when available, their tone is often dismissive or outright rude. Doors are shut during working hours while students wait outside, seeking basic assistance. Emails sent to official departments go unanswered, and technical issues plague even the simplest processes—from mark sheets to exam forms.
The quality of education, sadly, mirrors this dysfunction. There is little regard for student welfare, dignity, or timely resolution. The culture seems to prioritize internal comfort over public service, with staff enjoying leisurely breaks funded by student fees, while students struggle for clarity and support.
Mumbai University must urgently introspect and reform. Students deserve respect, transparency, and a functioning system—not bureaucratic indifference masked as procedure
